title: Check yourself: Stale results: the notice, the summary and the practice

questions.stem: An agent mapped a service of twelve modules on Friday. Over the weekend a developer rewrote two of them. On Monday the team resumes the session. What should the first prompt add?

options.text: A request to survey the whole service from scratch
options.says: Ruled out because naming the files is "targeted re-analysis rather than requiring full re-exploration", and a survey discards what the resume kept.

options.text: The paths that differ, with a request to re-read them
options.says: Naming the differing files gives targeted re-analysis and keeps everything still true.

options.text: Nothing at all, since the earlier read still holds
options.says: Ruled out because "Sessions persist the conversation, not the filesystem", so the weekend's edits are not in it.

options.text: The full text of both changed modules, pasted inline
options.says: Ruled out because the notice "does not paste the new contents: the session reads them with its own tools".

questions.stem: Most of the files an agent analysed last month have since been rewritten, and its transcript is long. Which start is most reliable?

options.text: A new run that begins by pasting the earlier tool output
options.says: Ruled out because a summary carries conclusions "never the raw tool output that went stale".

options.text: The full old transcript, with a line saying that things have changed
options.says: Ruled out because a notice can correct a few files but cannot correct most of them: "More than half of the analysed files changed or are gone, or the session was idle for more than 7 days" is the course's rule for starting fresh.

options.text: A fork of the transcript, so the original stays untouched
options.says: Ruled out because a fork "creates a new session that starts with a copy of the original's history", stale results included.

options.text: A new run that opens with a structured summary of the conclusions
options.says: When most results are stale, a summary of conclusions and their state is the reliable start.
